title: Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobli
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman calls him the leading sage of the generation in Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai’s time. In [Me’ilah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Meilah.17a.11-15), the government once decreed that they should not keep Shabbat and should not circumcise their sons, etc. Rabbi Reuven ben Itztrobli went and cut his hair in the komi style, went and sat with them, and through his wisdom the decree was annulled. Afterward they recognized that he was a Jew and decreed again, and they sent Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Yose to Rome to annul the decrees.

Two precious sayings of his remain to us: in [Moed Katan 18b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.18b.15-16) Rav said in his name, “From the Torah, from the Prophets and from the Writings [we learn] that a woman is [destined] for a man from the Lord”; and he further said there in his name: “A person is not suspected of something unless he did it,” etc.

In [Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.9.3.14), it is related that two sons of Rabbi Reuven Istrobilos were students of Rabbi. Rabbi saw that the Angel of Death was looking at them and gnashing his teeth. (Rabbi) said: “Let them be exiled to the South; perhaps exile atones.” When they came there, they died (for “a person’s feet…,” etc.).

notes.text: The komi style is a haircut. The linked Me’ilah episode relates the three decrees and their reinstatement. The names of the emissaries appear in the [continuation on 17b](https://www.sefaria.org/Meilah.17b.1). In Moed Katan, the second saying also has an alternative attribution directly to Rabbi Reuven in a baraita.

Hyman cites the end of Kilayim 9:4; the consulted passage is in 9:3. It has Rabbi see the Angel of Death looking at Reuven’s two sons. Rabbi proposes exile, and in the accompanying English the Angel of Death takes them there.
